And He subjected the sun and the moon (وسخر الشمس والقمر): meaning He made them subservient by continuing their revolution, so that life endures until its appointed term.

It is He who spread out the earth (هو الذي مد الأرض): meaning He spread it out so that life could exist upon it.

Firm mountains (رواسي): meaning stable mountains.

Two mates, two kinds (زوجين اثنين): meaning two types and two sorts, such as sweet and sour, yellow and black, for example.

Signs (لآيات): meaning proofs of the Oneness of Allah, the Exalted.

Adjacent tracts (قطع متجاورات): meaning adjoining plots of land.

Palm trees growing from one root or separately (ونخيل صنوان): meaning several palm trees sharing one root that gathers them. "Sinw" is the singular, and the plural is "sinwan".

In taste (في الأكل): meaning in flavor, this one is sweet, this one is bitter, this one is sour, and this one is delicious while that one is otherwise.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim-Ra﴾: Allah knows best what He intends by them. His words ﴿These are the verses of the Book﴾ refer to what came in the stories of Surah Yusuf. The "Book" here means the Torah and the Gospel, and among their verses is what Allah related to His Messenger. His words ﴿but most of the people do not believe﴾ mean that although what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, most people, both your own people and others, do not believe that it is the revelation and sending down of Allah, so that they might act upon it, be perfected and be happy.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿It is Allah who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see﴾: meaning, your true God, whom you must believe in, worship and declare as one, is Allah, who raised the heavens above the earth without visible pillars for you. Rather, He raised them by His power and by what He willed of laws. His words ﴿Then He established Himself upon the Throne﴾ mean He created the heavens and the earth, then established Himself upon His Throne in a manner befitting His essence and majesty, governing the affairs of the dominion. His words ﴿And He subjected the sun and the moon﴾ mean He made them subservient after creating them, so that they proceed in their orbits in an orderly course until the end of life. His words ﴿each runs [its course] to a specified term﴾ mean each travels in its orbit: the sun completes its orbit in a full year and the moon in a full month, and they continue thus until the end of the worldly life, when the moon will be eclipsed and the sun will be folded up. His words ﴿He arranges the affair﴾ mean He decrees what He wills in the heavens and the earth and governs the affairs of His creatures by causing death and life, withholding and giving, as He wills, alone, with no partner in this. His words ﴿He details the signs﴾ mean the Qur'anic signs, through recounting stories, presenting parables, and explaining what is lawful and unlawful. All of this is to prepare you and make you ready to believe in the meeting with your Lord, so that you believe in Him, worship Allah and declare Him one in worship, and are thereby perfected in your souls and morals and made happy in your worldly life and your Hereafter.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who spread out the earth﴾ meaning He extended it, ﴿and placed therein firm mountains﴾ meaning stable mountains, ﴿and rivers﴾ meaning He caused rivers to flow through it, ﴿and of all fruits He placed therein two mates, two kinds﴾ meaning two types and two sorts. Among pomegranates some are sweet and some are sour; among olives some are yellow and some are black; among figs some are white and some are red. His words ﴿He covers the night with the day﴾ mean that He, glorified and exalted, covers the day with the night for your benefit, so that you may sleep and your bodies may rest from the toil of the day.

His words ﴿Indeed in that﴾ refer to what is mentioned in this noble verse: the spreading out of the earth, the placing of the firm mountains in it, the causing of rivers to flow, the creation of varieties of fruits, and the covering of the night over the day. In all of what is mentioned, there are ﴿signs﴾, meaning clear indications and proofs of the existence of Allah, His knowledge, His power and His wisdom, and of the obligation to worship Him and declare Him one, and of belief in His promise and His warning, and in the meeting with Him, and in the bliss He has prepared for His friends and the punishment for His enemies.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And in the earth are adjacent tracts﴾ meaning plots of land, some adjoining others and close to one another. This one has good soil, and that one has bad soil, salty and barren. In the earth there are also gardens, meaning orchards of grapes, and in them crops and palm trees. ﴿Sinwan﴾: two or three palm trees sharing one root. ﴿Ghayru sinwan﴾: each palm tree standing on its own root. His words ﴿Watered with one water﴾ mean those grapes, crops and palm trees are irrigated with one water, ﴿yet We make some of them excel others in fruit﴾, which is what is eaten from them: this is sweet, that is sour, this is delicious, and that is insipid. His words ﴿Indeed in that﴾ refer to what was mentioned of the adjacent tracts, along with the difference in their goodness or lack of it, the gardens of grapes and palm trees, their being watered with one water, and the difference in their tastes, smells and benefits, are ﴿signs﴾, meaning clear and striking indications and proofs of the obligation to believe in Allah, declare Him one, and believe in the meeting with Him. But they are ﴿for a people who reason﴾. As for those who have lost their reason because matter has overcome it and desire has become firmly rooted in it, they do not perceive or understand anything. How then could they see the proofs of Allah's existence, His knowledge, His power and His wisdom, so that they might believe in Him, worship Him and draw near to Him?

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1. Affirmation of the doctrine of divine revelation and the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ).

2. Affirmation of the doctrine of Tawhid, that there is no god but Allah.

3. Affirmation of the doctrine of the Resurrection and of recompense for one's deeds in this world.

4. The virtue of reflecting upon the signs in creation.

5. The virtue of reason, by which one is guided to knowledge of the truth and to following it, for happiness and perfection.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 13, verses 5–9:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa in ta'jab* (وإن تعجب): that is, you are seized with wonder at their denial of your prophethood and of tawhid (monotheism).

*Fa-'ajab* (فعجب): that is, then I wonder at their denial of resurrection and the second life, despite the clarity of the evidences and the strength of the proofs.

*Lafi khalqin jadid* (لفي خلق جديد): that is, we will return as we were, living humans.

*Al-aghlal fi a'naqihim* (الأغلال في أعناقهم): that is, impediments preventing them from faith and guidance in this world, and shackles by which their hands will be bound to their necks in the Hereafter.

*Bil-sayyi'ah* (بالسيئة): that is, with the punishment.

His saying: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, that is, all that is hidden from creation and all that is not hidden of what they witness; the All-Knowing of everything. His saying: ﴿The Great, the Most High﴾, that is, the One greater than whom there is none, and before whom every great one is small; exalted over His creation, free of any partner, likeness, consort or offspring. **Explanation of the words (Sharh al-Kalimat):**

*Wa sarib bin-nahar*: that is, visible in his *sarb*, meaning his path.

*Lahu mu'aqqibat*: that is, angels who follow him by night and by day.

*Min amr Allah*: that is, by the command of God Most High, and with His permission and order.

*La yughayyiru ma biqawm*: that is, of well-being and blessing into affliction and punishment.

*Ma bi-anfusihim*: from purity and clarity through faith and acts of obedience to sins and transgressions.

*Wa ma lahum min dunihi min wali*: that is, they have no one other than God who will attend to their affairs and repel punishment from them.

*Min khifatihi*: that is, out of fear of Him, His awe and His majesty.

*Wa huwa shadid al-mihal*: that is, of strength and contest.

**Meaning of the verses (Ma'na al-Ayat):**

The context continues to speak of God's majesty, His great power and the breadth of His knowledge. God Most High says in this verse: ﴿It is the same whether any of you conceal speech or speak it aloud﴾; God knows the secret and the open, and what is more hidden. ﴿And whoever hides by night﴾ walks in its darkness, and whoever ﴿goes freely by day﴾, that is, walks in his path openly and in plain view of God Most High. As for His saying: ﴿For him are angels following him, before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of God﴾, it is permissible that the pronoun in "lahu" refers to the one who hides by night and goes freely by day. In that case, the *mu'aqqibat* are the guards and enforcers who protect the ruler, "by the command of God" in their view; but if God intends evil for someone, there is no repelling it, and he has no protector other than God who would defend him. It is also permissible that it refers to God Most High, and the *mu'aqqibat* are the angels who guard and record good and bad deeds; then "min amr Allah" means by His command and permission. The meaning is sound under both interpretations. Ibn Jarir adopted the first, and the majority of exegetes adopted the second.

As for His saying: ﴿And when God intends for a people an evil, there is no turning it back, and they have no protector other than Him﴾, this is an informing from Him, Most High, that when He intends for a people, an individual or a group some evil, that is, some affliction or punishment that will harm them, there is by no means any averting it; rather, it must befall them, and they will find no one other than God to turn away the punishment from them. As for God Most High, if they repent to Him, seek His forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance, He will remove the harm from them and avert the punishment.

This verse was indeed revealed concerning a man to whom the Messenger of God ﷺ sent someone to invite him to Islam. The disbelieving man said to the one who came from the Messenger of God ﷺ: "Who is the Messenger of God? And what is God? Is He of gold, of silver, or of copper?" Then a thunderbolt descended upon him while he was speaking, and it struck off the top of his skull. The meaning of "shadid al-mihal" is strength, seizing and striking.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 13, verses 14–16:

Explanation of the words:

*Lahu da'wat al-haqq* (لَهُ دَعْوَةُ ٱلْحَقِّ): That is, to Allah belongs the true call, i.e., He is the true God, there is no god but Him.

*Liyabligha fahu* (ليبلغ فاه): That is, the water reaches his mouth.

*Illa fi dalal* (إلا في ضلال): That is, in loss, with no gain obtained from it.

*Bil-ghuduwwi wal-asal* (بالغدو والآصال): That is, in the early mornings, plural of *bukrah* (بكرة), and the evenings, plural of *'ashiyyah* (عشية).

Meaning of the verses:

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 13, verses 17–18:

Explanation of the words:

Fa-sālat awdiyatun bi-qadarihā (فسالت أودية بقدرها): according to the measure of their water that flows in them.

Zabadan rābiyan (زبداً رابياً): a high-rising foam, for zabad (foam) is the scum produced by the boiling of water or by its flowing in rivers.

Wa-mimmā yūqidūna ʿalayhi fī al-nār (ومما يوقدون عليه في النار): such as gold, silver and copper.

Ibtighāʾ ḥilyatin aw matāʿ (ابتغاء حلية أو متاع): seeking an ornament of gold or silver, or an article of utensils.

Zabadun mithluh (زبد مثله): like the foam of the torrent.

Fa-ammā al-zabad (فأما الزبد): the foam of the torrent or the foam of what is heated upon the fire.

Fa-yadhhabu jufāʾ (فيذهب جفاء): as something false, cast away and far off, for it is scum and dross with no good in it.

Fa-yamkuthu fi al-arḍ (فيمكث في الأرض): it remains in the earth for a time from which people benefit.

Li-lladhīna istajābū li-rabbihim al-ḥusnā (للذين استجابوا لربهم الحسنى): for those who believed and did righteous deeds, the Garden.

Lam yastajībū (لم يستجيبوا): they did not believe in Him and did not obey Him.

La-iftadaw bihi (لافتدوا به): to ransom themselves from the punishment.

Sūʾ al-ḥisāb (سوء الحساب): being called to account for every sin they committed, of which nothing will be forgiven them.

Wa-bi'sa al-mihād (وبئس المهاد): the bed they prepared for themselves, which is Hell.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to establish tawhid and condemn disbelief and polytheism. In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted sets forth a parable of truth and falsehood: truth in its permanence, and falsehood in its vanishing and dissipation. He said: ﴿He sends down from the sky water, and the valleys flow according to their measure﴾, i.e., according to their size, for a valley may be large or small. ﴿So the torrent carries a swelling foam﴾, i.e., scum and high-rising dross upon the surface of the water. This is the watery parable. As for the fiery parable, the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And from that which they heat in the fire﴾, i.e., that which goldsmiths and smiths heat in the fire, ﴿seeking an ornament﴾, i.e., seeking ornament, ﴿or utensils﴾, i.e., seeking goods to enjoy such as vessels, for the goldsmith or smith places gold, silver or copper in the crucible and blows upon it with the bellows; what is corrupt and unfit rises up in the form of foam, while what is sound remains in the crucible, and it is from this that ornaments and utensils are made. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., of the four things mentioned, which are the two parables of truth, namely water and metal, and the two parables of falsehood, namely the foam of water and the foam of metal: ﴿As for the foam, it passes away as refuse﴾, i.e., cast away as falsehood, which the torrent throws to the bank of the valley, where it clings to trees and stones, and which the goldsmith casts off from his crucible; but what benefits people of water for irrigation remains in the earth, and likewise what benefits of ornaments and utensils remains in the crucible of the goldsmith and smith. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Thus Allah sets forth parables﴾, i.e., like this parable which He set forth for truth in its permanence and falsehood in its passing away and vanishing, even if it rises and overflows at times, ﴿He sets forth﴾, i.e., among the parables, ﴿that they may know, and believe, and be guided, and be perfected, and be happy.

This is what the first verse [17] contains. As for the second verse [18], Allah the Exalted has informed of His promise and His threat: His promise for the people of His obedience, that for them is the best reward, the Garden; and His threat for the people of disobedience, which is the most evil and severest threat. He said in His promise: ﴿For those who responded to their Lord is the best [reward]﴾, and He said in His threat: ﴿And those who did not respond to Him—if they had all that is in the earth entirely, and the like of it with it—they would surely offer it as ransom.﴾ i.e., of wealth and goods, ﴿and the like of it with it﴾ also, ﴿to ransom themselves from the punishment contained in this severe threat. He declares the threat, saying: ﴿Those—for them is the evil of account﴾, i.e., the wretched, ﴿and their refuge is Hell﴾, i.e., their abode and place of lodging, ﴿and wretched is the bed﴾, i.e., Hell is their bed.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The commendability of setting forth parables to bring meanings closer to minds.

2- The firmness of truth and the vanishing of falsehood is one of the sunan (laws) of Allah the Exalted.

3- Explanation of Allah's promise to those who respond to Him with faith and obedience, which is the Garden.

4- Explanation of Allah's threat to those who do not respond to Him with faith and obedience.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 13, verses 25–29:

Explanation of the words:

"Those who break the covenant of Allah" (wa-alladhina yanqudhuna ʿahda Allah): that is, they untie it and do not adhere to it, so they do not worship their Lord alone.

"And sever what Allah has commanded to be joined" (wa-yaqtaʿuna ma amara Allah bihi an yuwassala): that is, of faith and of the ties of kinship.

"And cause corruption on the earth" (wa-yufsidina fi al-ard): that is, by abandoning prayer and withholding zakat (obligatory almsgiving), and by committing evil deeds and neglecting good ones.

"For them is the curse" (lahum al-lacna): that is, distance from the mercy of Allah, exalted is He.

"And for them is the evil abode" (wa-lahum su' al-dar): that is, Hell, and wretched is the resting place.

"And He straitens" (wa-yaqdiru): that is, He restricts and constricts.

"Except a fleeting enjoyment" (illa matāʿ): a small amount enjoyed for a time, then it comes to an end.

"Blessed for them and a good return" (tuba lahum wa-husna maʾab): that is, for them is Tuba, a tree in Paradise, and a good destination, which is the Abode of Peace.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Most High, "And those who break..." (wa-alladhina yanqudhuna), etc., present the opposing party or the second figure, namely the one who has not known and has not believed, such as Abu Jahl, the opponent of Hamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib (may Allah be pleased with him). Here the Most High mentions the attributes that make them deserving of His punishment and deprivation, and so He mentions for them and for those of their kind the following attributes:

(1) Breaking the covenant, by not worshipping Allah and not affirming His oneness; this is the covenant taken from them in the world of souls: "And those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation" (wa-alladhina yanqudhuna ʿahda Allah min baʿdi mithaqihi).

(2) Severing what Allah has commanded to be joined, of faith and of the ties of kinship: "And sever what Allah has commanded to be joined" (wa-yaqtaʿuna ma amara Allah bihi an yuwassala).

(3) Causing corruption on the earth through polytheism and sins: "And cause corruption on the earth" (wa-yufsidina fi al-ard). By these attributes they have deserved this recompense. The Most High said: "Those—for them is the curse," that is, distance from mercy, "and for them is the evil abode," that is, Hell, and wretched is the resting place.

As for the words of the Most High: "Allah extends provision to whom He wills and straitens [it for whom He wills], and they rejoice in the worldly life, while the worldly life, compared to the Hereafter, is but a fleeting enjoyment" (Allah yabsutu al-rizqa li-man yasha'u wa-yaqdiru wa-farihu bi-al-hayat al-dunya wa-ma al-hayat al-dunya fi al-akhira illa matāʿ): He informs of one of His customs regarding His creation, namely that He extends provision, that is, widens it for whomever He wills, as a test whether he will give thanks or disbelieve, and straitens and constricts it for whomever He wills, as a trial whether he will be patient or despair. He may extend provision to some, since nothing but that would suit them, and He may straiten it for others, since nothing but that would suit them. Thus wealth is not a sign of Allah's pleasure, nor is poverty a sign of His wrath upon His servants.

As for His words, "and they rejoice in the worldly life" (wa-farihu bi-al-hayat al-dunya): those disbelievers rejoiced in the worldly life because of their ignorance of its measure, its outcome, and its evil effects. The worldly life, compared to what Allah has prepared for His friends, who are the people of faith in Him and obedience to Him, is but a little enjoyment, like a handful of dates or a loaf of bread given to a shepherd as food for him all day, which then runs out.

As for the words of the Most High in verse [27]: "And those who disbelieve say: Why has a sign not been sent down upon him from his Lord?" (wa-yaqulu alladhina kafaru lawla unzila ʿalayhi ayatun min rabbihi): such a demand has already been mentioned from the polytheists, namely their demanding of the Prophet ﷺ that there be for him a sign like the she-camel of Salih or the staff of Musa, so that they might believe in him, while they were liars in this. Only mockery and obstinacy led them to this demand, for the verses of the Qur'an are greater than the sign of the she-camel and the staff. Therefore the Most High said to His Messenger: "Say: Indeed Allah leads astray whom He wills" (qul inna Allah yudillu man yasha'), that is, He leads him astray, even if he sees and witnesses thousands of signs, "and guides to Him those who turn back" (wa-yahdi ilayhi man anaba), even if he has not seen a single sign, provided he turns back to Allah; so He guides him to Himself, accepts him, and makes him among His close friends.

As for the words of the Most High in verse [28]: "Those who believe, and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah" (alladhina amanu wa-tatmainnu qulubuhum bi-dhikr Allah): those who turned back to Him in faith and monotheism, He guided them to Him on a straight path. These are the ones whose hearts find rest, that is, become settled and at ease, in the remembrance of Allah, in the remembrance of His promise, and in the remembrance of His righteous servants, Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. And the words of the Most High: "Surely in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest" (ala bi-dhikr Allah tatmainnu al-qulub), that is, the hearts of the believers; as for the hearts of the disbelievers, they find rest in the remembrance of worldly things and its pleasures, and the hearts of the polytheists find rest in the remembrance of their idols.

As for the words of the Most High: "Those who believe and do righteous deeds—for them is Tuba, and a good return" (alladhina amanu wa-ʿamilu al-salihati tuba lahum wa-husnu maʾab): this is an announcement from Allah, the Most High, of what He has prepared for the people of faith and righteous deeds. Tuba is a state of goodness and pleasantness that eloquence cannot describe, or a tree in Paradise, and a good return, which is Paradise, the Abode of Peace and everlasting bliss.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The prohibition of adopting the attributes of the people of wretchedness, namely breaking the covenant, severing what Allah has commanded to be joined, and causing corruption on the earth through polytheism and sins.

2- Clarification that wealth and poverty occur according to the knowledge of Allah, the Most High, as a test and trial; they indicate neither Allah's pleasure nor His wrath.

3- The lowliness of this world and the meagerness of its enjoyments.

4- The virtue of the remembrance of Allah and the tranquility of the heart in Him.

5- Allah's promise to the people of faith and righteous deeds of Tuba and a good return.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 13, verses 30–32:

Explanation of the words:

"Kadhalika arsalnaka" (Thus We have sent you): that is, in the same manner as that sending by which We sent Our messengers, We have sent you.

"Litatlua 'alayhim" (That you may recite to them): that is, that you may recite to them the Qur'an as a reminder, a teaching, a warning and a glad tiding.

"Wa hum yakfuruna bi'l-Rahman" (While they disbelieve in the Most Merciful): when they said, "What is al-Rahman?" and said, "There is no Rahman except Rahman of al-Yamamah."

"Suyyirat bihi'l-jibal" (If by it the mountains were moved): that is, removed from their places.

"Aw qutti'at bihi'l-ard" (Or the earth were split asunder by it): that is, cleft so that rivers and springs were made.

"Aw kullima bihi'l-mawta" (Or the dead were made to speak by it): that is, they were brought to life and spoke.

"Afalam yay'as" (Has not despaired): that is, has not known.

"Qari'ah" (A calamity): that is, a disaster that strikes their hearts with fear and sorrow and destroys and uproots them.

"Aw tahullu qariban min darihim" (Or it settles near their dwellings): that is, the calamity, or the Islamic army.

"Fa-amlaytu" (Then I gave respite): that is, I gave them time and delayed them for a long period.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to establish the foundations of belief: monotheism, prophethood, resurrection and the final recompense. In the first verse of this context, His saying, ﴿Thus have We sent you﴾, He affirmed the prophethood of the Messenger (ﷺ) by saying "thus," meaning the sending which We sent before you, to a nation before which other nations have passed. He explained the purpose of the sending, saying: ﴿that you might recite to them that which We have revealed to you﴾, which is mercy, guidance and healing, ﴿while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful﴾, the Most Merciful who sent you to them with guidance and the religion of truth for their perfection and happiness; they disbelieve in Him. Then say, O Messenger: ﴿He is my Lord; there is no god but Him. In Him I have put my trust and to Him is my return﴾, that is, my repentance and my return. Thereby He established the principle of monotheism in the most truthful expression.

As for His saying, in the second verse [31], ﴿And if only a Qur'an by which the mountains were moved﴾ etc.: there is no doubt that the polytheists of Makkah were demanding from him what is mentioned in this verse, for they said: "If you are a messenger, then pray to your Lord to remove for us these mountains that surround our valley, so that our land may expand for planting and tilling, and split our land so that You bring forth for us springs and rivers, and bring back to life for us so-and-so and so-and-so, so that we may speak with them and ask them about the truth of what you say and claim, that you are a prophet." So He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if only a Qur'an had by it the mountains been moved, or the earth been split by it, or the dead been made to speak by it﴾, meaning this Qur'an would have done so. But signs do not guide; rather, the command belongs entirely to Allah: He guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills. Since Allah, the Exalted, turned them away from the cosmic signs, knowing that if He gave them these, they would not believe in them, the punishment of annihilation would be due upon them like the previous nations. Some of the believers used to wish for the cosmic signs, supposing that if the polytheists witnessed them they would believe and the battle raging between polytheism and monotheism would end. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Have not those who believe despaired﴾, that is, known, ﴿that had Allah willed, He would have guided all people﴾ by signs and without them. So let the matter be left to Him, glorified and exalted, to do what He wills and decree what He desires. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And disaster will not cease to strike those who disbelieve for what they have done﴾, that is, of polytheism and sins, ﴿a calamity﴾, that is, a disaster that strikes their hearts with fear and dread and their souls with worry and sorrow, such as drought, sickness, killing and captivity, ﴿or it will settle near their dwellings﴾, that is, the Messenger will alight with his Islamic army to conquer Makkah, until the promise of Allah comes, giving you victory over them, O Messenger. The verse is general concerning those after Quraysh, and the threat encompasses the nations of disbelief in general; and behold, wars strike them every generation once or twice, and the atomic war is at their doors, and their affair remains thus until the Islamic army alights near their dwellings, so that they enter the religion of Allah or perish. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise﴾, and He has fulfilled what He promised Quraysh.

In the last verse [32], the Exalted informs His Messenger, consoling him for the hardship and pain he endures from the arrogance and obstinacy of the polytheists, saying to him: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked﴾, that is, just as you are mocked, so they were patient, so be patient as well. ﴿Then I gave respite to those who disbelieved﴾, that is, I granted them time and reprieve until the proof was established against them, then I seized them and left none of them. ﴿So how was My punishment?﴾, that is, it was severe, all-encompassing and fell in its proper place. Likewise I shall do to those who mock you, O Our Messenger, if they do not repent and submit.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of monotheism.

2- No reliance except upon Allah, and no repentance for anyone except to Him.

3- The greatness of the noble Qur'an and the explanation of its virtue.

4- The use of the word "despair" meaning "knowledge."

5- The Exalted Lord threatens the disbelievers with calamities in this world until the Day of Resurrection.

6- Allah, majestic in His majesty, gives respite and delays, but He does not neglect; rather He seizes and punishes.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 13, verses 33–35:

Explanation of the words:

"Afaman huwa qa'imun 'ala kulli nafsin bima kasabat" (Is then He who stands over every soul in what it has earned): i.e., its Guardian, its Provider, the One who knows it and what it has earned, and who recompenses it for its deeds.

"Qul sammuhum" (Say: Name them): i.e., describe them to Him: who are they?

"Am tunabbi'unahu bima la ya'lamu" (Or do you inform Him of what He does not know?): i.e., do you inform Him of what He does not know?

"Bi-zahirin min al-qawl" (With an outward saying): i.e., with a false assumption that has no reality in fact.

"Ashaqq" (more severe): i.e., more intense.

"Waqin" (protector): i.e., one who prevents them from the punishment.

"Mathalu al-jannah" (The likeness of the Garden): i.e., its description which We relate to you.

"Ukuluha da'imun wa ziluha" (Its food is everlasting and its shade): i.e., what is eaten therein is everlasting and never perishes, and its shade is everlasting and is never abrogated.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues in establishing monotheism and refuting polytheism, through the saying of the Exalted: "Afaman huwa qa'imun 'ala kulli nafsin bima kasabat", i.e., its Guardian, its Provider, the One who knows it and what it has earned of good and evil, and who recompenses it, is like one who neither guards, nor provides, nor knows, nor recompenses, and that is the idols. Thus their worship is refuted, and nothing remains but the true God, Allah, there is no god but He and no lord besides Him. And the saying of the Exalted: "Wa ja'alu lillahi shuraka'a", i.e., they worship them alongside Him. "Qul sammuhum", i.e., say to them, O our Messenger: Name for us those partners; describe them, show us who they are? "Am tunabbi'unahu bima la ya'lamu fi al-ardi", i.e., do you inform Allah of what He does not know on earth? "Am bi-zahirin min al-qawl", i.e., rather, with an outward saying, that is, with a false assumption that has no reality in fact.

And the saying of the Exalted: "Bal zuyyina lilladhina kafaru makruhum", i.e., their false saying and their deceitful fabrication was made attractive to them, and by it they were turned away from the way, the way of truth, and were diverted from it so that they did not find guidance to it. "Wa man yudlili Allahu fama lahu min hadin." And the saying of the Exalted: "Lahum 'adhabun fi al-hayati al-dunya", by killing and captivity, "Wa la 'adhabu al-akhirati ashaqqu", i.e., more severe than the punishment of this world, whatever it may be. "Wa ma lahum min Allahi min waqin", i.e., they have no one besides Allah who will protect them, turn it away from them, and repel it so that they will not taste it. And the saying of the Exalted: "Mathalu al-jannati allati wu'ida al-muttaqun", i.e., when He mentioned the punishment of the Hereafter for the people of disbelief and wickedness, He mentioned the bliss of the Hereafter for the people of faith and piety, saying: "Mathalu al-jannati allati wu'ida al-muttaqun", i.e., the description of the Garden. He described it with His saying: "Tajri min tahtiha al-anharu, ukuluha da'imun wa zilluha", everlasting likewise; its food does not run out, and its shade does not vanish nor is it abrogated by a sun like the shade of this world. And His saying: "Tilka", i.e., the Garden, "'Uqba alladhina ttaqaw", i.e., their Lord; so they believed in Him, worshipped Him, affirmed His oneness, and obeyed Him in His commands and prohibitions. "Wa 'uqba al-kafirina al-naru." And 'uqba means the outcome, in good and in evil.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

﴿Who deny part of it﴾: that is, part of the Qur'an. The polytheists denied the name "al-Rahman" and said, "There is no al-Rahman except the Rahman of al-Yamamah," meaning Musaylimah the liar.

﴿And thus have We sent it down as an Arabic judgment﴾: that is, in the tongue of the Arabs, so that you may judge among them by it.

﴿For every term there is a Book﴾: that is, for every period there is a Book in which the appointed term is written.

﴿Allah erases what He wills﴾: that is, He erases some of the rulings and other things and confirms what He wills. What He erases is the abrogated (mansukh), and what He leaves is the established (muhkam).

The context continues to establish the foundations of belief: monotheism (tawhid), prophethood, resurrection and recompense. The polytheists denied "al-Rahman" and said, "There is no al-Rahman except the Rahman of al-Yamamah," meaning Musaylimah the liar, may the curses of Allah be upon him. In this is an affirmation of monotheism. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And thus have We sent it down as an Arabic judgment﴾: that is, just as We sent down the Qur'an, We sent it in the tongue of the Arabs so that you may judge among them by it. In this is an affirmation of divine revelation and of Muhammad's prophethood. His saying: ﴿And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you﴾, by agreeing with them in their religions and their falsehood in belief. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And We have certainly sent messengers before you and given them wives and offspring﴾: so there is no sense in what the deniers say: "Why did Muhammad not take wives and why does he have no offspring?" when he says that he is the prophet and messenger of Allah. The messengers before you, from Noah and Abraham to Moses, David and Solomon, all had wives and offspring. He is the Owner and the Disposer: if He wills, He gives them, and if He wills, He withholds from them. His saying: ﴿For every term there is a Book﴾: that is, for every appointed time in which Allah gives or withholds, there is a Book in which that term was written and specified, so there is no disorder and no chance. His saying: ﴿Allah erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾: this is a response to their saying that a matter is not established and then cancelled, such as the change of the direction of prayer from Jerusalem to the Kaaba, and the waiting period from a year to four months and ten days. He informed them that Allah, Exalted is He, has a will and a volition that are not subject to the wills and volitions of people. He erases from the laws and rulings what He wills according to the needs of His servants, and likewise confirms what is good and beneficial for them. ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾: that is, the Book that contains all the decrees, so no alteration or change enters it, such as death and life, happiness and misery. Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Affirmation of the doctrine of revelation and prophethood.

2- Affirmation of the doctrine of monotheism.

3- Affirmation that the primary source of judgment and rule in Islam is the noble Qur'an, then the Sunnah as its explanation, then permitted analogy (qiyas), then the consensus of the Ummah, since it is impossible for it to agree on anything other than what Allah loves and is pleased with.

4- Warning against following the people of innovation, desires, and false creeds and sects (milal wa-nihal).

5- Affirmation of the doctrine of divine decree and destiny (qadar).

6- Explanation of abrogation (naskh) in the rulings, by the Book and the Sunnah.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 13, verses 40–43:

Explanation of the words:

"Nu'iduhum" (We promise them): i.e., of the punishment.

"Aw natawaffayannaka" (or We take you in death): i.e., before that.

"Nanquṣuhā min aṭrafihā" (We reduce it from its outlying parts): i.e., country after country, through conquest and the entry of Islam into it and the ending of polytheism in it.

"Lā mu'aqqiba li-ḥukmihi" (none can reverse His judgment): i.e., none can repel it, so that His judgment is not overturned and rendered void.

"Wa man 'indahu 'ilm al-kitab" (and whoever has knowledge of the Book): from among the believers among the Jews and Christians.

Meaning of the verses:

His Exalted saying: ﴿And whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We take you in death﴾, meaning: if We show you some of the punishment with which We threaten your people, so be it; and if We take you in death before that, then upon you is only the conveyance (of the message). You have conveyed it, and upon Us is the reckoning; so We will recompense them for what they earned. So do not grieve, O Messenger, and do not be distressed by what they plot. His saying ﴿Do they not see﴾ means: the polytheists, the deniers, the schemers, who demand signs as proof of the truthfulness of the prophethood of our Prophet ﴿that We come to the land, reducing it from its outlying parts﴾, meaning: We open it to Islam, country after country. Is that not a sign indicating the truthfulness of the Messenger ﷺ and the soundness of his call?

His saying: ﴿And Allah judges; there is none to reverse His judgment﴾, meaning: and Allah, Majestic and Exalted, judges among His creation as He wills; He honours and humiliates, gives and withholds, grants victory and defeat. "None can reverse His judgment" means there is no one who can review His judgment and nullify it. So when He judges that Islam shall prevail and disbelief shall retreat, who could reverse that for Allah?

His saying: ﴿And He is swift in reckoning﴾: when He calls to account for what is earned, His reckoning is swift, recompensing the doer according to what he deserves, without delay or postponement.

His exalted saying: ﴿And those before them had already schemed﴾, meaning: nations before the Quraysh and the disbelievers of Makkah had schemed. So how was the outcome of their scheming? Indeed, it was their total destruction. Do the leaders of disbelief in Makkah not fear such an outcome?

His saying: ﴿To Allah belongs all scheming﴾, meaning: therefore their scheming carries no weight and has no value; it should not be feared or heeded.

His saying: ﴿He knows what every soul earns﴾, of good and evil. How can the scheming of one who does not know be compared with the scheming of One who knows everything? He will bring the one schemed against to the brink of ruin while he is unaware. Will the disbelievers of Quraysh not take this to heart, and desist from their scheming against the Messenger of Allah and his call?

His exalted saying: ﴿And the disbelievers will know to whom belongs the final abode﴾, meaning: the polytheists, the opponents of monotheism, will know on the Day of Resurrection to whom belongs the good final outcome, namely the one who enters Paradise, Muhammad ﷺ and his followers, or to whom belongs the Fire, namely the callers to polytheism and disbelief and their followers.

His exalted saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger."﴾ meaning: they confront you with denial and reject your prophethood and messengership. Say to them, O Messenger: "Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you," and He has testified to my messengership and sworn to it several times in His speech, such as ﴿Yā-Sīn. By the wise Qur'an, indeed you are among the messengers﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 1–3]. And the testimony of Allah is sufficient testimony.

﴿And whoever has knowledge of the Book﴾: the first being the Torah and the Gospel, namely the believers among the People of the Book, from the Jews and Christians, such as 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Salman al-Farisi, al-Najashi, Tamim al-Dari, and others.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The victory and spread of Islam within a quarter of a century is the greatest proof that it is the truth.

2- The judgments of Allah are not to be reversed, and it is not permissible to seek appeal against any judgment of Allah the Exalted in His Book or in the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ.

3- The testimony of Allah is the greatest testimony, so no further testimony is to be sought after it when the dispute is between believers.

4- The virtue of the knowledgeable over the ignorant, for the testimony of the believing People of the Book establishes the proof against those among the polytheists who lack knowledge.
